title: Seats says which provider is running on what credential, and a real codex seat delivers
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-969575299465484d9486ea02ff7ae336 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605, the setting) and child 2 (task-df64aa204d6f4c35810376226980e4b7, mission parity). PROOF ROW: it owns the UI, the Playwright journey, the live drive and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the provider toggle in the browser, the Seats screen showing provider + credential SOURCE + CLI version per seat, the missing-credential refusal rendered verbatim, and the live `codex exec` drive.

CREDENTIAL SOURCE, NEVER A VALUE. Seats shows WHERE the credential came from - a sign-in file, or the NAME of an env var - and never the value itself. `moe-up-credentials.ts` / `moe-up-env.ts` hold the CODEX_HOME / CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN / OPENAI_API_KEY / CODEX_API_KEY roster, and the launcher's `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` roster is what renders when the chosen provider has no credential. This is the one clause in this row worth a hostile test: a credential in an operator's screenshot cannot be recalled.

THE LIVE DRIVE MAY LEGITIMATELY BE BLOCKED. The parent filed this row while the Codex quota was exhausted until 2026-09-08, and its DoD 4 says so explicitly: if the quota still refuses, `moe.report_blocked` with the RESET DATE and the EXACT refusal line - never a fabricated pass. That is a real outcome, not a failure of this row.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: `KNOWN_PROVIDERS = ["claude","codex"]` at apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts:34; the Seats panel renders under `data-testid="cr.sessions.root"` in apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-screens.tsx, fed by live-sessions.ts, whose decoder is EXACT-KEY (it refuses a response whose key set differs) - so any new member on /sessions/read needs the daemon and the decoder to move together, or the Seats screen goes blank. task-92d84d384e4443d7bf78c76024af5688 is also extending /sessions/read (with the concurrency limit); expect a rebase there.
definitionOfDone: A provider toggle in the browser writes the durable setting from child 1, and the Seats screen shows PROVIDER, CREDENTIAL SOURCE and CLI VERSION per seat, read from a REAL daemon frame.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS EVER RENDERED - only its source (a sign-in file, or an env var NAME). Assert it hostilely: a frame carrying a credential-shaped value renders the source only, and the test greps the rendered output for the value and finds nothing. A credential in an operator screenshot cannot be recalled.

When the chosen provider has NO credential, the launcher's `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` roster renders VERBATIM, naming which variables are missing - an operator whose seats will not start needs the variable names, not 'no credential'.

The env override from child 1 is visible here: with `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` set, Seats says the effective provider AND that a launcher env override is in force, so a browser choice that is being ignored is legible rather than mysterious.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon covers the toggle and the Seats reading, with the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. The /sessions/read decoder is EXACT-KEY: daemon and browser move together, and a round-trip assertion proves it.

LIVE DRIVE: a real `codex exec` seat delivers a node on UnAI or a fresh project - transcript and landing sha in a row comment under ~4500 chars. IF THE CODEX QUOTA STILL REFUSES, report_blocked with the reset date and the EXACT refusal line (the parent's DoD 4 makes this a legitimate outcome) - never a fabricated pass, and never a claude seat reported as a codex one.

docs/agent-stack-runbook.md 'Codex seats' and the README Codex clause ('wired but was last proven only to reach the API') are updated to the measured truth. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: NEVER RENDER A CREDENTIAL VALUE - only its source. This is the row's one hard safety property and it carries its own hostile test.

A BLOCKED LIVE DRIVE IS AN ACCEPTED OUTCOME when the Codex quota refuses: report_blocked with the reset date and the exact refusal line. Never fabricate a pass and never report a claude seat as a codex one.
THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD: if the setting does not reach the spawn, that is child 1's; if a codex seat cannot complete its mission, that is child 2's. Comment there and report_blocked.
/sessions/read has an EXACT-KEY browser decoder and another row (task-92d84d38) is extending the same read; daemon and browser move together, and expect a rebase.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description: MEASURE AND BASELINE. NO EDITS. THIS ROW WAS NARROWED - read this before the description. Two deliverables were carved out because the row's own rail 3 says "THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD" while its DoD asked for surfaces that do not exist: (a) the per-seat PROVIDER and CLI VERSION members on /sessions/read are now task-adc4b229cae840c086cc1acc83fd4989, declared in dependsOn; (b) the LIVE `codex exec` drive is now task-117a3cd91a8a4db1a61830be8c28f2d2, because a vendor quota blocking it would otherwise have stranded landed browser work. THIS ROW IS THE BROWSER PROOF and it is quota-free. Where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY. (b) CONFIRM THE PREREQUISITES, at the tree not the board: `grep -n 'agentProvider' apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts` (task-3958769c's project-scoped member) and the per-seat members from task-adc4b229; `git grep -n 'set_agent_provider' apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` for the kind the toggle dispatches. Any absent, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds naming it. Read their completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings for exact member names rather than retyping them here. (c) THE CREDENTIAL-SOURCE HALF IS ALREADY BUILT AND ALREADY SAFE - do not rebuild it, and read its header before touching anything nearby. `apps/control-room/src/v2/resources/resources-credential.ts` is documented as "THE ONE PLACE THE PROVIDER'S CREDENTIAL IS TURNED INTO SOMETHING RENDERABLE": a CLOSED grammar `credential/<leaf>/(env:<VAR>|login-file|ungated)`, failing closed to `RESOURCES_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED`, plus `credentialSourceWords()`. Its header explicitly warns against a SECOND SCRUB. `resources-model.ts:136-158` shows the composition to copy: build from `credentialSource()` alone, read no other field of the receipt. REUSE those exports; a second grammar here would be the exact defect that module was written to prevent. (d) BASELINE (global rail 3), standalone foreground, quoting each count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`. Any red is FOREIGN and pre-existing; quote it so step 5 can subtract it. (e) `git status --porcelain -- apps/ docs/ README.md tests/` and note peer dirt; never revert it.

THE TOGGLE. The browser writes the durable provider setting. Find the dispatch path first rather than inventing one: `apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch.ts` is the seam and `live-dispatch-payloads.ts` holds the caller-half payloads, re-exported at live-dispatch.ts:27 - the header there records that the payloads live in ONE roster on purpose, so add the `project.set_agent_provider` body there and never spell a literal at the call site. THE PROVIDER NAMES COME FROM ONE ROSTER: `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` at apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts:34 is `["claude", "codex"]`, frozen, with a docblock saying claude is named first so a tie is decided there rather than in the browser. The control room cannot import apps/daemon (no workspace edge; a deep relative import is TS6059), so the browser holds a transcription - if one already exists, reuse it; if you must add one, add a test that pins it against the daemon roster the way live-sessions.test.ts:63-75 pins the sessions frame by SOURCE TEXT, so a third provider cannot appear on one side alone. Render the control in the Seats/ops area under a `cr.` test id consistent with its neighbours (`cr.sessions.*` at activity-screens.tsx:118-146). KEEP THE PRODUCTION FILE UNDER 250 LINES (row rail 5) - activity-screens.tsx is 181, so a toggle component of any size belongs in its own module rather than growing it. ASCII-ONLY SOURCES AND APOSTROPHE-FREE JSX TEXT (row rail 5): the scheduler package-boundary scan reds on an apostrophe in JSX, so write "the operator has not chosen" and never "operator's choice" in rendered text.

THE SEATS DISCLOSURE, AND THE ONE HARD SAFETY PROPERTY. New module under apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ (target well under 250 lines), rendered from activity-screens.tsx. FOUR THINGS TO SHOW, each from a surface that already exists after the prerequisites: the seat's PROVIDER and CLI VERSION (task-adc4b229's per-seat members); the CREDENTIAL SOURCE, composed from `credentialSource()` / `credentialSourceWords()` exactly as resources-model.ts:143-153 does; and the ENV OVERRIDE (task-3958769c's `agentProvider.envOverride`), rendered so an operator whose browser choice is being IGNORED can see why - DoD-4's point is that a silently overridden choice is mysterious, so name the override, do not merely flip a label. THE SAFETY PROPERTY, DoD-2, is the row's one hard requirement and it is structural rather than a matter of care: build the rendered string from the CLOSED grammar's OUTPUT only - `parsed.cli` and `credentialSourceWords(parsed.source)` - and never from the ref, never from any other field of the receipt, never from a raw daemon string. A ref the grammar does not recognise yields null and the caller states the refusal code where the source would have gone; that is the file's designed failure mode, RENDERING LESS, and it is what makes the hostile test in step 4 pass by construction rather than by vigilance. WHEN THE CHOSEN PROVIDER HAS NO CREDENTIAL (DoD-3): render the launcher's `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` roster VERBATIM, naming which variables are missing. It is exported from apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-env.ts:26 (re-exported from moe-up-credentials.ts) - again unimportable from the browser, so find the frame that already carries it to the browser and read it there; if NO daemon read publishes that roster, STOP AND REPORT rather than inventing a second copy of the variable names in the browser, because two rosters drift and the operator would be told to set a variable the launcher does not check. An operator whose seats will not start needs the NAMES, not "no credential".

TESTS, WITH THE HOSTILE ONE FIRST. (1) THE CREDENTIAL TEST, DoD-2, and the only one in this row that guards a property that cannot be walked back: feed a frame whose credential ref carries a CREDENTIAL-SHAPED VALUE where the source belongs, render, then GREP THE RENDERED OUTPUT FOR THAT VALUE and assert zero occurrences. Assert positively too - that the refusal code appears where the source would have gone - so the arm cannot pass merely because nothing rendered at all. Use a value that would be obvious in a screenshot (a long random-looking token), and note in a comment WHY the arm exists: a credential in an operator's screenshot cannot be recalled. `resources-screen.test.tsx:167-169` is the existing shape for driving `credentialSource` with hostile refs. (2) The toggle writes the durable setting: assert the DISPATCHED PAYLOAD and its command kind, not that a click handler fired. (3) The missing-credential case renders the variable NAMES verbatim from the roster, not a generic phrase - assert on a name. (4) The env-override case says both the effective provider AND that a launcher override is in force. (5) A PLAYWRIGHT JOURNEY against a REAL daemon (DoD-5) covering the toggle and the Seats reading, in tests/e2e/control-room/. Read `mem:control-room-production-bundle-serves-fixtures-on-a-url-param` before writing it - the production bundle serves fixtures on a url param, and a journey that accidentally reads fixtures proves nothing about the daemon. The /sessions/read decoder is EXACT-KEY, so include the round-trip assertion DoD-5 asks for: the daemon's real frame decodes and renders, which is what proves daemon and browser moved together.

DOCS, DRILLS, GATES, SELF-REVIEW. (a) DOCS (DoD-7), and they must be reduced to the MEASURED truth, not to intent: `docs/agent-stack-runbook.md` "Codex seats", and the README clause at :137 which currently reads "a Codex seat is wired but was last proven only to reach the API". THAT CLAUSE IS STILL TRUE AFTER THIS ROW and must not be rewritten as though it were not - the live `codex exec` drive is task-117a3cd9 and has not run. Update both to say exactly what is now proven: the browser can choose a provider, Seats discloses it with its credential SOURCE, and a scripted double drives the real MCP wire (task-ae309e47) - while the real-binary drive remains outstanding, naming that row. Overstating here would retire a question nobody answered. (b) DRILLS. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST; the Playwright spec is NEW and untracked, so `git diff` is BLIND to it - SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup (%TEMP%, suffixed by worker id) in a call SEPARATE from the restore. The tracked files take an empty `git diff`. Say which proof applies to which path. THREE DRILLS: (i) make the credential renderer read the raw ref instead of the grammar's output - the DoD-2 grep arm must go RED and the leaked value must appear in the failure output. That is the drill that proves the safety property is real; run it carefully and quote it. (ii) Drop the env-override rendering - the DoD-4 arm reds. (iii) Replace the verbatim `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` names with a generic phrase - the DoD-3 arm reds naming the missing variable name. (c) GATES - standalone foreground, one per call, no pipes and no `;` chains, quoting each `Test Files N passed` count line: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (MANDATORY - most of this row lives there and no other leg sees it), `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for apps/**. `pnpm test:e2e:browser` runs `tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` FIRST - a tsc failure is not a test result. Attribute red by failing paths at HEAD minus the step-1 baseline, intersected with this row's owned paths. Named complete_task verification command: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. (d) ADVERSARIAL PASS on this diff only: grep your own diff for any path that renders a daemon string directly into the credential slot; a ref the grammar refuses (does the screen show the code, or blank); a seat whose provider disagrees with the project-level `agentProvider.effective` - which does the operator see, and is that legible; an apostrophe in JSX text or a non-ASCII character (the scheduler boundary scan reds on both); any production file over 250 lines; a toggle click while a seat is mid-run. (e) COMPLETION RECORD must state: that the credential SOURCE is composed from the landed closed grammar and no second grammar was written; that the per-seat members are task-adc4b229's and the env-override member is task-3958769c's, both verified by grep at the delivered tree; that the README's "last proven only to reach the API" clause was deliberately NOT retired, naming task-117a3cd9 as the row that will retire it; and drill (i) verbatim, since it is the proof of this row's one hard safety property.

SPLIT THREE WAYS: THE ROW'S RAIL 3 AND ITS DoD-1 CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER. architect-b63fabf3, 2026-09-05, HEAD f3b94eaa. Plan approved: 5 steps, 4 files. Where description and plan disagree, THE PLAN IS AUTHORITY.

## The contradiction, measured part by part

Rail 3 says "THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD". DoD-1 required Seats to show PROVIDER, CREDENTIAL SOURCE and CLI VERSION per seat. I checked all three separately:

| | state |
|---|---|
| **credential source** | **already built and already safe** — `resources-credential.ts`, a closed grammar, fed by the activation receipt through `live-activation.ts` |
| **per-seat provider** | **does not exist** — task-3958769c's `agentProvider` is a *project*-scoped frame member; `SessionView` has no provider |
| **CLI version** | **does not exist anywhere** — `git grep -rn '\-\-version' -- apps/daemon/src` finds no agent-CLI probe |

So two thirds of DoD-1 would have forced this row to build production surface its own rail forbids, on the same exact-key frame two other rows are already moving. Rail 19 forbids answering that with a narrowed DoD.

## The cut

- **`task-adc4b229`** (new, order 72.6, dependsOn task-3958769c) — the per-seat provider and CLI version on /sessions/read, plus the decoder in lockstep. Production, so this row can stay a proof row. It carries the design question I would not delegate: whether the version is captured at spawn and written durably, or probed at read time — the daemon cannot observe a child it did not spawn, and `configuredAgentLimit` three lines away is the precedent for naming that limit honestly.
- **`task-117a3cd9`** (new, order 73.5) — the live `codex exec` drive. Cut on the PATH axis because its blocking condition is **external and dated**: the quota was exhausted until 2026-09-08, and DoD-6 sanctions `report_blocked` for it. Left here, that outcome would have blocked the toggle, the Seats rendering, the Playwright journey and the docs sweep too — stranding four landed deliverables behind a vendor quota.
- **This row** — the browser proof, now quota-free and landable. `dependsOn` rewired to `[8e793ae3, df64aa20, adc4b229]`.

## Do not rebuild the credential grammar — it is what makes DoD-2 pass by construction

`resources-credential.ts` is documented as *"THE ONE PLACE THE PROVIDER'S CREDENTIAL IS TURNED INTO SOMETHING RENDERABLE"* and its header warns explicitly against **a second scrub**. Its grammar is closed, fails to `RESOURCES_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED`, and its own comment notes an env var NAME is upper snake case while an API credential is not — *"so the grammar cannot match a value even if one is substituted for the name"*. Compose `credentialSource()` / `credentialSourceWords()` the way `resources-model.ts:136-158` does, and DoD-2's hostile test passes **structurally** rather than by vigilance. Drill (i) proves it: make the renderer read the raw ref and require the grep arm to red with the leaked value visible.

## Two rosters cannot cross the package boundary

`KNOWN_PROVIDERS` (health-read.ts:34) and `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` (moe-up-env.ts:26) both live in apps/daemon, and the control room cannot import it — no workspace edge, deep relative import is TS6059. A retyped copy drifts silently, and for the missing-credential roster the drift would **tell an operator to set a variable the launcher does not check**. The plan requires reading it off a frame, or stopping and reporting if no daemon read publishes it.

## The README clause stays true

README:137 — "a Codex seat is wired but was last proven only to reach the API" — is **still true after this row**; the real-binary drive is task-117a3cd9. The docs sweep must say what is now proven and name that row for the rest. Retiring it here would retire a question nobody answered.

One stale premise corrected: the description says task-92d84d38 is "also extending /sessions/read… expect a rebase". That row is DONE; the live contention is now task-3958769c and task-adc4b229.

planningNotes.risks:
